title: Auditors’ findings on federal money the City passed on, and what the City did next
question: When a grantee’s auditors report a finding on federal money that came through the City, does the City’s own monitoring that year show it, and does the money change?
finding: 16 audits of 11 City-paid organizations for fiscal years ending 2019 to 2025 carry a finding on a programme the City passed through; 6 involve a material weakness, questioned costs or a repeated finding. In 4 of the 16 the City’s monitoring for the same year records no findings, a waiver or an unfinished review (PRC 2022: monitoring not complete; PRC 2024: no findings; Compass Family Services 2019: no findings; Shanti Project 2022: monitoring waived). Examples: Eviction Defense Collaborative Inc fiscal 2024 (1 material weakness, 1 with questioned costs, 0 repeated; City paid $25.0 million, then $21.6 million); Baker Places Inc fiscal 2021 (0 material weakness, 0 with questioned costs, 2 repeated; City paid $18.0 million, then $19.4 million); PRC fiscal 2021 (0 material weakness, 0 with questioned costs, 2 repeated; City paid $4.8 million, then $5.5 million); Mission Action Inc fiscal 2021 (1 material weakness, 0 with questioned costs, 0 repeated; City paid $10.6 million, then $13.1 million).
how: Clearinghouse findings joined to the award line they cite; kept where the auditor names the City as the pass-through body for that line. The City’s monitoring result is the Controller’s fiscal and compliance monitoring for the same fiscal year (published for fiscal 2019 and 2022 to 2025). City payments are the payment-table figure for the audit year and the two years after.
limits: A finding is the auditor’s statement of a control weakness or an unsupported cost, not a finding of loss; many are corrected within a year and the audit’s own corrective-action plan says how. What the City, as the body that passed the money on, did about each finding is not in the published files. City monitoring looks at different standards on a different calendar, so a clean monitoring year beside an audit finding is a question, not a contradiction. For the fiscal years covered here, the federal audit threshold depends on the start of the entity’s fiscal year. It was $750,000 in federal awards expended across all programs for years starting before October 1, 2024, and $1 million for years starting on or after that date. An entity reaches the threshold at either amount. City payments alone cannot establish how much federal funding the recipient expended.
